# Story 22 — Demo data seeders across every module, idempotent, wired into the restart script (Story: 514)

## Prerequisites

- Story 2.2 (users, roles, departments) delivered — `backend/app/Modules/Security/` including `EloquentDepartmentDirectory`, `Roles`, `Department` domain, `UsersController`, `DepartmentsController`.
- Story 3.1 (customer record) delivered — `backend/app/Modules/Customers/` including `Customer`, `CustomerSearch`, `ContactIdentifier`, `IdentifierNormaliser`, `DuplicateDetector`.
- Story 3.2 (notes and attachments) delivered — `CustomerNote` and `backend/app/Modules/Platform/Attachments/Application/AttachmentUploader.php`.
- Story 4.1–4.4 (ticket create, assign, lifecycle, history, conversation, internal notes) delivered — all commands under `backend/app/Modules/Tickets/Domain/Commands/`.
- Story 6.1 (portal identity) delivered — `backend/app/Modules/Portal/Domain/PortalAccount.php` + migration `2026_09_05_000500_link_portal_accounts_to_customers.php`.
- Existing precedent to match tone: `backend/database/seeders/DevAccountsSeeder.php` — same environment guard and idempotent write shape must be reused.
- Coordinate with owners of `scripts/restart.sh` (shared dev tooling) before adding a new mandatory `db:seed` step outside the `migrate:fresh --seed` path.

---

## Story Goal

A single `php artisan db:seed` on a freshly migrated (or existing) local/testing database produces a complete, realistic, deterministic and idempotent dataset across every implemented module so that agent home, ticket list, ticket detail, customer profile, timeline and the admin console are all non-empty on first sign-in. The three existing staff accounts survive unchanged; three additional agents, six-plus customers, five-plus bilingual categories, eighteen-plus tickets (covering all statuses/priorities/channels), two-plus attachments and two-plus portal accounts appear. Ticket writes go **only** through the Tickets module commands (AD-3). References come from their allocators. `scripts/restart.sh` runs the seed on the fresh, `--no-fresh` and `--wipe-volume` paths, skips it under `--no-seed`, and aborts the run with a named error on failure.

**Not in scope:** SLA and Email seed data (no tables). No `settings` rows (Story respects AD-5 — settings resolve from registry defaults). No new schema, no new HTTP endpoints, no UI.

## Product rules (from story)

- **Idempotent by natural key.** Every seeder short-circuits when data already exists. Natural keys: department name, user email, category `name` (English), customer `reference`, ticket `reference`, contact identifier (kind + normalised value), portal account email.
- **Deterministic.** Fixed names, emails, subjects; any RNG carries a fixed seed; timestamps are relative to `now()`.
- **Local development only.** Same guard as `DevAccountsSeeder`: skip with warning outside `['local', 'testing']`.
- **Runnable in isolation.** Each seeder `$this->call()`s whatever it depends on (like `DevAccountsSeeder` already does with `RolesAndPermissionsSeeder`).
- **AD-3.** No `DB::table('tickets')->insert(...)`, no `DB::table('ticket_events')->insert(...)`, no Eloquent `Ticket::create(...)` inside the seeders. All ticket writes go through commands under `backend/app/Modules/Tickets/Domain/Commands/`.
- **AD-5.** No writes to the `settings` table.
- **Reference allocators.** `TicketReferenceAllocator` and the customer reference allocator are resolved from the container; never hard-code.

- Build a **fixed catalog** of ≥ 18 ticket blueprints hard-coded in a `private function blueprints(): array` method. Every blueprint carries a **stable subject** used as the idempotency key. Distribution constraints (must all be satisfied by the fixed list):
  - Every one of the three seeded agents (`agent@ragab.test`, `agent.support@ragab.test`, `agent.sales@ragab.test`, `agent.billing@ragab.test`) is the assignee of ≥ 2 tickets.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Re-run on live data.** Every seeder must be safely re-runnable — enforced by natural-key lookup before write. Any seeder that would otherwise `create()` unconditionally is a bug; verify by asserting row counts in the double-run test (see Test Plan).
- **Isolated run with missing prerequisites.** Each demo seeder calls `$this->call(...)` for its dependencies so `php artisan db:seed --class=Database\\Seeders\\DemoTicketsSeeder` on a fresh DB succeeds. Mirrors the existing `DevAccountsSeeder.php:65` pattern.
- **Production/staging invocation.** Environment guard warns and returns without writing. Verified by feature test that sets `App::environment` to `production`.
- **Reference collision.** After seeding, application-created tickets/customers must not reuse a seeded reference. Because references are drawn from the allocator (sequence-backed), correctness depends on the seeder never hard-coding a reference — enforce with a `grep` in the double-run test that scans `DemoTicketsSeeder.php` and `DemoCustomersSeeder.php` for hard-coded reference-like literals matching the format seen in `TicketReference.php`.
- **Attachment partial state.** Row present but file missing (developer wiped `storage/app/attachments/`): seeder detects and rewrites the file only; row is left in place. See Task 8.
- **Ambient auth in commands.** Every command call passes an explicit `Actor`. `tests/Architecture/CommandsDoNotReadAmbientAuthTest.php` scans modules, not seeders, so the discipline is enforced by review; the double-run test additionally asserts no `Auth::user()` / `auth()->user()` string appears in any `Demo*Seeder.php` file.
- **Bypassing tickets write path.** Direct `DB::table('tickets')->insert(...)` in a seeder would corrupt versioning and skip event append. The double-run test greps every `Demo*Seeder.php` file for `'tickets'` and `'ticket_events'` in string context and fails on match.
- **Settings shadowing.** Writing any `settings` row from a demo seeder would violate AD-5. Guard by a grep in the test.
- **Portal login without link.** `PortalAccount.customer_id` must not be null for seeded rows (dev-only demo). Assert in test.
- **RTL data.** Bilingual categories must round-trip Arabic without mojibake. Assert one Arabic string exactly.
- **Slow seed.** Full seed must complete under 60 s. Include a soft assertion (`< 30 s`) in the double-run test with a comment permitting relaxation up to 60 s.
- **`--no-seed` flag.** `scripts/restart.sh` must skip `run_seed` entirely; verify by dry-running the script with `--no-seed` and confirming no `db:seed` line appears in the trace.
- **Half-migrated DB.** If migrations fail before seed, the script already aborts; ensure `run_seed` is only invoked on the success branch of the migration step.

## Migration / Rollback

- No schema change. No migration file added.
- Rollback: revert the `DatabaseSeeder.php` diff and delete the new `Demo*Seeder.php` files plus the two fixture binaries; restore the original `scripts/restart.sh`.
- Half-applied risk: because every seeder is idempotent and guarded, a partial run leaves at worst a subset of expected rows; re-running converges. No destructive operations are performed.

---

## Verification Steps

1. **Backend builds:** in `backend/`, `composer install` (if needed) then `php artisan config:clear && php artisan migrate:fresh && php artisan db:seed`. Expect the summary lines from each seeder and completion in under 60 s.
2. **Idempotency by hand:** run `php artisan db:seed` a second time. Expect no error and row counts unchanged (confirm with `php artisan tinker` snippets: `\App\Models\User::count()`, `\App\Modules\Tickets\Domain\Ticket::count()`, `\App\Modules\Customers\Domain\Customer::count()`).
3. **Isolated seeder:** `php artisan db:seed --class=Database\\Seeders\\DemoTicketsSeeder` on an already-seeded DB — expect zero writes.
4. **Guard:** `APP_ENV=production php artisan db:seed --class=Database\\Seeders\\DemoDepartmentsSeeder` — expect the `skipped` warning and zero writes.
5. **Backend tests:** in `backend/`, `php artisan test --filter=Seeding` and then the full `php artisan test`.
6. **Restart script — fresh:** `./scripts/restart.sh` — expect migrations, seed, summary block.
7. **Restart script — no-fresh:** `./scripts/restart.sh --no-fresh` — expect seed to run once and be a no-op on second invocation.
8. **Restart script — wipe-volume:** `./scripts/restart.sh --wipe-volume` — expect seed to run after volumes are re-provisioned.
9. **Restart script — no-seed:** `./scripts/restart.sh --no-seed` — expect no `db:seed` line in the output; row counts remain zero after fresh.
10. **Restart script — failure surfacing:** temporarily break a seeder (throw in `DemoDepartmentsSeeder::run`), rerun the script, confirm it aborts with `SEED_FAILED` and shows the tail of the seed output. Revert.
11. **Frontend smoke:** in `frontend/`, `pnpm dev`, sign in as `admin@ragab.test` / `Correct-Horse-9`. Confirm agent home shows counts, ticket list is non-empty across every filter combination, ticket detail shows messages and events, customer profile shows identifiers and (for ≥ 2) notes, admin console shows the three demo departments and five bilingual categories, and downloading a ticket attachment and a customer attachment both succeed.
12. **Portal smoke:** sign in with a seeded portal account (email from `DemoPortalAccountsSeeder`, password `Correct-Horse-9`) and confirm a portal-channel ticket is visible.
13. **Regression:** `php artisan test` (backend) and `pnpm test` (frontend) — both green.

---

## Done Criteria

- [ ] Freshly migrated DB after `php artisan db:seed` has non-empty `departments`, `users`, `ticket_categories`, `customers`, `contact_identifiers`, `customer_notes`, `tickets`, `ticket_messages`, `ticket_events`, `attachments`, `portal_accounts`.
- [ ] `admin@ragab.test`, `super@ragab.test`, `agent@ragab.test` present with unchanged roles; 3 additional agents present, each with `department_id` and `is_active = true`.
- [ ] Every seeded agent assignee of ≥ 2 tickets; ≥ 2 tickets unassigned.
- [ ] All 4 `TicketStatus`, `Priority`, `TicketChannel` values represented across the seeded tickets.
- [ ] Every seeded ticket carries ≥ 2 messages; ≥ 3 tickets carry ≥ 1 internal note.
- [ ] Every seeded ticket carries the history events its lifecycle implies (verified by counting rows in `ticket_events` and asserting at least `created` + `assigned` (where applicable) + `status_changed` (where applicable)).
- [ ] No `Demo*Seeder.php` file writes to `tickets`, `ticket_events`, `ticket_messages` or `settings` directly (architecture test green).
- [ ] Ticket and customer references obtained from allocators; a fresh application-issued reference after seed continues the sequence without collision (continuity test green).
- [ ] Running `db:seed` twice leaves row counts identical for every table listed above (idempotency test green).
- [ ] Each `Demo*Seeder` is runnable in isolation via `--class=...` on a clean DB and self-bootstraps its dependencies.
- [ ] Running any `Demo*Seeder` outside `local`/`testing` writes zero rows and logs a skip message (guard test green).
- [ ] Two consecutive full runs produce identical names, emails, references and subjects (determinism verified by comparing snapshots).
- [ ] Two attachments exist (one ticket-owned, one customer-owned), both `ScanStatus::CLEAN`, with files present on disk under the configured attachments disk; both downloadable via the existing signed-URL flow.
- [ ] Two portal accounts exist, `verified_at` non-null, `customer_id` linked, sign-in with `DevAccountsSeeder::PASSWORD` succeeds.
- [ ] `settings` table row count is 0 after full seed.
- [ ] `scripts/restart.sh` runs the seed on the fresh, `--no-fresh` and `--wipe-volume` paths; skips it under `--no-seed`; aborts with `SEED_FAILED` and a readable log on failure; prints a counts summary on success.
- [ ] Automated test asserts the double-run row-count invariant.
- [ ] Full seed completes in under 60 s on a normal dev machine (record time in test output).
- [ ] `.squad/DEV-CREDENTIALS.md` lists the three new agent emails.

**STOP HERE. Report to the user and wait for confirmation before proceeding to the next story.**
